at pakke.explanation: "At pakke" means "to pack". When you put your things in a bag, say: "Jeg pakker tasken" (I am packing the bag). When you wrap a present, add "ind": "Jeg pakker gaven ind" (I am wrapping the present). When you mean a parcel, the noun "en pakke" is spelled the same: "Jeg henter en pakke" (I am picking up a parcel).

at pakke ud.explanation: "At pakke ud" means "to unpack". It is built from "at pakke" (to pack) and "ud" (out). When you take your things out of a bag, say: "Jeg pakker tasken ud" (I am unpacking the bag). When you open a present, it is also used: "Børnene pakker gaver ud" (The children unwrap presents).

at parkere.explanation: "At parkere" means "to park". When you leave a car somewhere, say: "Jeg parkerer bilen her" (I am parking the car here). When you read a sign that forbids parking, you see the noun: "Parkering forbudt" (No parking).

at passe.explanation: "At passe" means "to fit (suit)". When clothes are the right size, say: "Skoene passer mig" (The shoes fit me). When a time is good for you, it means "to suit": "Mandag passer mig godt" (Monday suits me well). When you take care of a child, it means "to look after": "Jeg passer min lillebror" (I am looking after my little brother).

at passe børn.explanation: "At passe børn" means "to babysit". It is built from "at passe" (to look after) and "børn" (children). When you look after an animal, the same verb works: "at passe en hund" (to look after a dog).

at passe ind.explanation: "At passe ind" means "to fit in". When a person feels part of a group, say: "Han passer godt ind på holdet" (He fits in well on the team). When a thing looks right in a room, say: "Sofaen passer ind i stuen" (The sofa fits into the living room).

at passe på.explanation: "At passe på" means "to take care / watch out". When you warn someone about danger, say: "Pas på!" (Watch out!). When you wish someone well, say: "Pas på dig selv" (Take care of yourself). When you look after someone's object, say: "Jeg passer på dine nøgler" (I am looking after your keys).

at passe til.explanation: "At passe til" means "to go with / suit". When two pieces of clothing match, say: "Skjorten passer til bukserne" (The shirt goes with the pants). When a job is right for a person, say: "Jobbet passer til dig" (The job suits you).

at passere.explanation: "At passere" means "to pass". When you go past a place, say: "Vi passerer banegården" (We are passing the train station). To say you pass a test, use "at bestå" (to pass an exam) instead: "Jeg bestod prøven" (I passed the test).

at pege.explanation: "At pege" means "to point". When you point at something, use "på" (on) after the verb: "Han peger på bilen" (He points at the car).

at pege på.explanation: "At pege på" means "to point to". It is built from "at pege" (to point) and "på" (on). Danish keeps "på" where English says "to" or "at": "Han peger på bogen" (He points to the book).

at pendle.explanation: "At pendle" means "to commute". When you travel to work every day, say: "Jeg pendler til København" (I commute to Copenhagen). A person who does this is "en pendler" (a commuter).

at piske.explanation: "At piske" means "to whisk / whip". When you beat cream with fast strokes until it gets stiff, say: "Jeg pisker fløden" (I am whipping the cream).

at pjække.explanation: "At pjække" means "to skip school / play hooky". When you stay away from school without permission, say: "Han pjækker fra skole" (He is skipping school). Use "fra" (from) to name what you skip.

at placere.explanation: "At placere" means "to place". When you put something in a spot, say: "Jeg placerer vasen på bordet" (I put the vase on the table). When you give a guest a seat, say: "Jeg placerer dig her" (I will seat you here).

at plage.explanation: "At plage" means "to pester / torment". When a child keeps asking a parent for something, say: "Børn kan plage deres forældre om slik" (Children can pester their parents for candy). When pain or noise bothers a person again and again, say: "Smerterne plager ham" (The pain torments him).

at planlægge.explanation: "At planlægge" means "to plan". It is built from "en plan" (a plan) and "at lægge" (to lay). When you prepare a trip ahead, say: "Vi planlægger en ferie" (We are planning a holiday).

at plante.explanation: "At plante" means "to plant". When you put vegetables in the ground, say: "Jeg planter tomater" (I am planting tomatoes). The noun "en plante" (a plant) is spelled the same: "Jeg vander min plante" (I am watering my plant).

at pleje.explanation: "At pleje" means "to usually (do) / to care for". When you say what you normally do, put "at" (to) and the action word after it: "Jeg plejer at gå tidligt i seng" (I normally go to bed early). When you look after someone who needs help, it means "to care for": "Hun plejer sin syge far" (She cares for her sick father).

at plukke.explanation: "At plukke" means "to pick", as in picking fruit or flowers. When you take apples off a tree by hand, say: "Børnene plukker æbler" (The children are picking apples). When you pull the feathers off a bird, it also means "to pluck": "at plukke en kylling" (to pluck a chicken).

at plyndre.explanation: "At plyndre" means "to plunder / loot". When thieves or soldiers take everything of value from a place, say: "De plyndrer byen" (They are plundering the town). When someone takes all the food from a place, it also means "to raid": "Børnene plyndrer køleskabet" (The kids raid the fridge).

at poste.explanation: "At poste" means "to post". When you put a message online, say: "Hun poster en kommentar" (She is posting a comment). When you send a letter, it means "to mail": "Jeg poster brevet i dag" (I am mailing the letter today).

at praktisere.explanation: "At praktisere" means "to practice", as in following a belief or working in a profession. To say what a person follows, say: "Hun praktiserer buddhisme" (She practices Buddhism). To say you repeat something to get better, use "at øve" (to practice) instead: "Jeg øver klaver" (I am practicing the piano).

at presse.explanation: "At presse" means "to press / pressure". When you squeeze juice out of fruit, say: "Jeg presser en appelsin" (I am squeezing an orange). When you push a person to do more, say: "Chefen presser os" (The boss is pressuring us).

at printe.explanation: "At printe" means "to print". When you print a page from a computer, say: "Jeg printer dokumentet" (I am printing the document). When a press prints books or newspapers, Danish uses "at trykke" (to print with a press): "De trykker aviser" (They print newspapers).
